subject.title: github-copilot: legacy OAuth token refresh sends bearer credential to unvalidated enterpriseUrl domain

question: Should the legacy GitHub Copilot OAuth refresh path reject, normalize, or repair non-allowlisted persisted `enterpriseUrl` values before sending any bearer refresh token?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the permanent behavior for already-persisted legacy credentials is a security-boundary and upgrade-compatibility choice that automation should not decide.

options.title: Fail closed plus doctor repair
options.body: Reject non-allowlisted domains in refresh and add a doctor fix that reports or rewrites unsafe legacy `enterpriseUrl` values before runtime uses them.

options.title: Runtime fallback only
options.body: Normalize unsafe domains to `github.com` at refresh time, which reduces token egress risk but leaves unsafe legacy state stored until later cleanup.

options.title: Private security workflow first
options.body: Move the follow-up into the repository security process before deciding the public migration and release behavior.

recommendation.title: Fail closed plus doctor repair
recommendation.body: Reject non-allowlisted domains in refresh and add a doctor fix that reports or rewrites unsafe legacy `enterpriseUrl` values before runtime uses them.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal for the current auth-profile and refresh code path points to this handle, and the decision crosses core auth migration policy.
